summary: Slice 0.5 MCGS Security foundation formally verified. 13/13 backend tests pass covering four-tier defence (Tier 1 alert at 3 fails, Tier 2 lockout at 5 fails with 429+Retry-After, Tier 3/4 mass-attack detector raising MCGS signal at 20+ fails), revocable JWT sessions with jti claim, /security/summary/events/sessions/lockouts endpoints, backwards-compat with /cms/admin-log and /cms/members, and clear-lockout cascade. Frontend Playwright verifies /admin/security page renders 4 numeric summary tiles, 6 tabs (overview/successes/fails/sessions/lockouts/password-changes), 'Ask George about security' top-right button, all 4 threshold tiers in the Thresholds section, sidebar Security link in System group with NO 'Soon' pill, and Sessions tab lists the admin's own session with a Revoke button. All test data cleaned up (admin_security_log, admin_login_attempts, admin_lockouts, admin_sessions, mcgs_signals with kind='security.mass_login_attempts' all show 0 residual rows for the test email + synthetic entries). NO REGRESSION on the existing login flow — real admin login continues to work and creates a session with jti.
critical_code_review_comments: cms_module.py is now 2970 lines — well past the 700-line comfort line. Consider splitting security endpoints (~130 lines) into a dedicated /app/backend/routes/cms_security.py. Not blocking Slice 0.5 sign-off, but on the tech-debt list.

services/security.py `session_is_valid` intentionally soft-accepts unknown jti (migration safety). Once every legacy pre-0.5 token has TTL'd out (12h JWT lifetime), consider flipping the soft-accept to a hard reject for defence-in-depth. Comment already in the code — flag for a follow-up ticket.
The /cms/security/lockouts/clear body is `dict` (untyped) rather than a Pydantic model. Minor — a Pydantic model would give a nicer 422 on malformed input instead of the 400 dance.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all UI acceptance points verified via Playwright)

seed_data_creation: None persisted. Test suite creates + cleans up per-run: TEST_EMAIL 'e2e-slice05@friendplace-test.dev' rows, 21 synthetic fail events for mass-attack detector, and admin sessions/logs from the test itself. Post-run collection counts for all test-created rows = 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Slice 0.5 security is green. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_slice05_security.py runs sync (pymongo, no pytest-asyncio needed) and is safe to re-run — it self-cleans before and after. Key sequencing subtlety: after triggering Tier 2 lockout on TEST_EMAIL, the requester's IP-scoped lockout ALSO exists (email + ip counters bump together). The test's cleanup step deletes recent IP-scoped rows so subsequent legitimate admin logins don't get 429'd. If pytest-asyncio ever gets installed, tests are already structured cleanly enough to swap in @pytest.mark.asyncio + motor without much churn.
rca_of_issue: No bug found — all verified as designed.
